images.title: Same unit, then take away
images.purpose: Show the one idea the student practises: re-cut both fractions into one common unit, then take away whole units, as in 5/6 − 1/3 = 5/6 − 2/6 = 3/6.
images.composition: Two strips of exactly the same length stacked with a wide gap, left edges lined up, and one equation line centred below.
images.exact_structure: Top strip, one whole: cut by solid lines into 3 equal parts, each split by one grey #6B7280 dashed line into 2, making 6 equal small parts; the 2 leftmost small parts are filled amber #E69F00. Bottom strip, the same length: cut into 6 equal parts lined up with the top strip; the 5 leftmost are filled teal #0072B2, and of these the 4th and 5th have a thick reddish purple #CC79A7 outline and are drawn lifted slightly above the strip. Exactly 2 strips, 12 small parts, 2 amber, 5 teal, 2 lifted.

images.takeaway: Make the units the same, then take away.
images.description: A strip in thirds re-cut into sixths shows 1/3 = 2/6; a strip of 5/6 has 2 sixths lifted away, leaving 3/6, which is 1/2.
images.context: Shown with the doer concept before the student practises. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say why the amber third is counted as two sixths before any piece is lifted away.

image_decisions.why: One clean picture of re-cutting into a common unit and lifting units away primes the practice.
